description:
Create a new intent from the user's request and mark it as active for THIS session.

Call this when check_active_intent returns no active intent for your session. Before calling:
1. Summarize what the user is asking for
2. Ask the user to confirm the intent details (title, description, type)
3. Then call this tool with the confirmed details

This ensures all AI-generated code gets properly tracked and attributed.

Multi-active model: many intents can be active on a repo at once (one per
session/teammate). Creating + activating one only sets YOUR session's current
focus — it never blocks or displaces another session's active intent.

If the new intent overlaps existing work, YOU do not decide what happens: Kawa
Code parks the request, asks the user, and this tool reports the outcome in
"action". An overlap parks a decision for the user — it is not an instruction to
stop working. Act on "action":
- "created" / "reactivated": done; the intent is active. Proceed.
- "pending_approval": the user has been asked in Kawa Code; the intent does not
  exist yet. Tell them it is waiting, keep working on anything that does not
  depend on this intent, and call this tool again with the returned pendingId
  (same title, description and repoPath) at your next checkpoint or once they
  say they have answered. Each call waits up to ~20 seconds for the answer.
- "awaiting_user": this tool will stop asking. Do not sit idle — a parked request
  expires after 24 hours and is dropped when the session ends, so the answer you
  would be waiting for may never come. Tell the user, continue independent work,
  and call once more with the pendingId after they say they have answered.
- "declined": the user said no to this intent. Do not retry it under another
  title. Edits already on disk are not reverted — tell the user and ask what
  they want done with them.
- "expired" / "unknown_pending": nothing was decided; call again without pendingId
  if the work is still wanted.
Work done while a request is parked is still real work, but it is not attributed
to the intent: decisions recorded before the intent exists carry no intent id,
and complete_intent has nothing to complete until it does. So continue, but reach
the decision before you commit. There is no force option — only the user can
decide an overlap.

If this tool call itself times out (before any pendingId was returned), call it
once more with the same arguments — it will not create a duplicate request.

constraints.description: Requirements or constraints for this work

pendingId.description: Only after a pending_approval response: the pendingId it returned. Asks whether the user has decided. Pass the same title, description and repoPath as before.

repoOrigin.description: Git remote origin URL. Auto-detected from repoPath via git if not provided.

repoPath.description: Local path to the repository root

title.description: Short, descriptive title for the intent

name: create_and_activate_intent
